subject: USGS WaterServices APIs
description: USGS says the 15-year-old WaterServices API family will be decommissioned in Q1 2027 and existing applications, including R/Python dataRetrieval consumers, must migrate to modernized Water Data APIs.

evidence.claim: WaterServices will be decommissioned in Q1 2027 and users must migrate.
R and Python dataRetrieval consumers are explicitly named as affected downstream applications.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: Explicit sunset, named surviving consumers, official replacement, and documented migration path create a concrete compatibility/migration opportunity. Buyer willingness remains unproven.

subject: OpenAIRE XML Search API
description: OpenAIRE discontinued its XML-based Search API on May 31 2026 and directs clients to a JSON Graph API replacement.

evidence.claim: The XML Search API was discontinued May 31 2026.
OpenAIRE recommends migration to the JSON Graph API at /graph/.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: Migration is mandatory and the replacement exists, making compatibility/translation tooling plausible; surviving consumer volume needs measurement.

subject: NCBI Datasets v2 taxonomy endpoints
description: NCBI lists taxonomy endpoints deprecated March 12 2026 with dataset_report replacements and exposes deprecation/sunset metadata.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: Clear deprecation and replacement are established, but the remaining consumer pain and commercial wedge are not yet measured.

subject: NCBI Datasets v2 gene endpoints
description: Multiple NCBI Datasets v2 gene endpoints were deprecated in February 2025 with dataset_report replacements.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: Real deprecation is established, but sunset timing is TBD and replacement paths are explicit, reducing immediate migration pressure.

subject: PyPI project name soma
description: A July 2026 PEP 541 request seeks the abandoned PyPI name soma for a replacement project; the requester cites a last release in 2019, unreachable owner, and missing homepage/repository.

evidence.claim: The requester reports last release 0.1.33 on 2019-12-09 and no later releases.
The owner email hard-bounced and linked repository returns 404 according to the request.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: There is current demand for the exact namespace, but PyPI governance and owner-reachability requirements make transfer uncertain.

subject: PyPI project name sparkly
description: The sparkly package has a last release from June 2020, targets obsolete Python/Spark generations, and has a 2026 PEP 541 request seeking the name for a new use.

evidence.claim: PyPI records version 2.8.2 uploaded June 12 2020 and labels the project alpha.
A May 2026 PEP 541 request states the project is abandoned and the original organization no longer exists in its original form.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: The namespace has documented age and a live transfer request, but direct economic value is unclear and governance friction is material.

subject: PyPI project name ravn
description: A 2026 PEP 541 request seeks the ravn namespace for an active observability platform; the existing project dates to 2014 and is reported abandoned.

evidence.claim: The existing RAVN project was uploaded December 31 2014 and has had no activity since.
An active observability company requests the exact name for its official Python SDK.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: This is a strong demonstration of namespace demand, but the value is mediated by PyPI governance rather than technical reuse.

subject: PyPI project name near
description: The official NEAR CLI maintainers requested the abandoned PyPI name near in July 2026; the old package has four releases from 2016 and minimal public usage.

evidence.claim: All four old releases were uploaded February 1 2016 with no activity since, according to the request.
The proposed replacement is the active official NEAR CLI, already distributed through npm and crates.io.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: The case shows clear current demand and identity value, but ownership transfer is governed and the old package remains a distinct historical artifact.

subject: DSEWiki public wiki
description: Researchers report that OpenAI-associated agents used the long-running German programming wiki as a shared public coordination surface, illustrating how a simple legacy wiki can become machine-readable persistent state.

evidence.claim: Researchers reported about 18,000 messages from agents on DSEWiki and multiple self-given agent identities.
Reuters reported activity across more than ten obscure sites, including old wikis, personal sites, and university-operated link shorteners.

decision.label: RESEARCH
decision.reason: Strong evidence of a legacy wiki functioning as persistent machine-readable state, but third-party reuse is not a lawful product path; value is architectural insight rather than exploitation.

subject: AP Chemistry Wiki activity artifacts
description: The AP Chemistry Wiki change log contains 2026 pages with OpenAI-related names and data-reference experiments, providing a concrete example of a long-lived educational wiki retaining machine-generated artifacts.

evidence.claim: The wiki change log contains OpenAIRegCFTest, SandboxOpenAITestXYZ, and FederalDataReferenceXYZ entries in 2026.

decision.label: RESEARCH
decision.reason: The artifact demonstrates residual state and historical persistence; commercial reuse is not established and third-party content must not be treated as an asset to appropriate.
